title: Design cache eligibility and object identity
description: Choose a route and cache-key policy, then change traffic and freshness. The model exposes origin relief, object fragmentation, and unsafe sharing of private responses.

routes.label: Public product catalog
routes.detail: Mostly shared GET responses with a bounded language dimension.

routes.label: Search results
routes.detail: Public responses, but query combinations create a larger object space.

routes.label: Signed-in account page
routes.detail: The response contains user-specific identity, balances, or permissions.

policies.label: Pass every request
policies.detail: Safest default while the response contract is unknown; no shared object is stored.

policies.label: Hash URL only
policies.detail: High reuse, but unsafe when authorization, session, or representation headers change the body.

policies.label: Pass auth, vary approved dimensions
policies.detail: Pass authenticated requests, remove tracking noise, and vary only language or encoding when required.

policies.label: Hash every cookie
policies.detail: Avoids sharing sessions, but analytics and experiment cookies create many cold variants.

notice: This is a teaching model, not a Varnish benchmark. Real hit rate depends on request distribution, object size, cache capacity, eviction, TTL, invalidation, and VCL behavior measured from Varnish logs.
